elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without Vendor consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (d) expressly states that the consent requirement does not apply to an assignment by Sparkling to an affiliate; paragraph (c) is conformed by the phrase “or as permitted by this Agreement.”

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (d) expressly exempts an assignment by Sparkling to a successor in a merger from the consent requirement.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (d) expressly exempts an assignment by Sparkling to a successor in an acquisition from the consent requirement.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (d) expressly exempts an assignment by Sparkling to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets from the consent requirement.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign this Agreement without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The unchanged opening sentence of paragraph (d) requires the other party’s written consent, and no exception is provided for an assignment by Garman.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The added sentence states that “Sparkling's consent to an assignment by Garman shall not be unreasonably withheld.”

elements.element: Vendor may never assign this Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The added sentence states categorically that “Garman may not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Sparkling.”

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement because of a change of control of Customer.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly states that a change of control of Sparkling does not give Garman any right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Sparkling may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer must give Vendor written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No operative provision requires Sparkling to give Garman written notice of a successor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The consent exception applies only to Sparkling. Garman remains subject to Sparkling’s written consent for successor assignments.

elements.element: Vendor must give Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No operative provision creates a written-notice mechanism for a successor assignment by Garman.

elements.element: For Customer assignments other than to a successor, Vendor consent is required.
elements.evidence: Sparkling may also assign to an affiliate without Garman’s consent, even where that affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor's consent to a Customer assignment other than to a successor may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard applies only to Sparkling’s consent to an assignment by Garman; no equivalent restriction applies to Garman’s consent.

elements.element: For Vendor assignments other than to a successor, Customer consent is required.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (d) requires Sparkling’s written consent for every assignment by Garman, including assignments other than to a successor.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment other than to a successor may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Although the clause generally says Sparkling’s consent may not be unreasonably withheld, it categorically prohibits every assignment by Garman to a Sparkling competitor. Thus the fallback’s reasonableness standard does not govern all non-successor assignments.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred position, and the paragraph (c) cross-reference prevents the separate assignment restriction from negating Sparkling’s new exceptions. The fallback is not satisfied because there is no mutual successor-assignment right on written notice, Garman receives no reasonableness protection for Sparkling’s non-successor assignments, and Garman has no successor exception. The redline is targeted and coherent, though the broad paragraph (c) cross-reference could have been drafted more narrowly to refer specifically to assignment permissions.
